title: Small actions accumulate
idea: Repeat a useful action before chasing a dramatic result.
example: Practise one keyboard shortcut each morning instead of redesigning your whole workflow.
action: Repeat one tiny improvement today.
scene: An adult practising one keyboard shortcut at a calm desk; calendar pages change and the task becomes smoother.
narration: Repeat a useful action before chasing a dramatic result. Repeat one tiny improvement today.

title: Build evidence for your identity
idea: Small actions make a new self-image more believable.
bullets: Choose who you want to become.
example: Someone who wants to be considerate puts their phone away during one conversation.
action: Choose one action that supports your desired identity.
scene: An adult sets down a phone, listens carefully to a friend and smiles.
narration: Small actions make a new self-image more believable. Choose one action that supports your desired identity.

title: Understand the habit loop
idea: Look for the signal, desire, action and payoff behind a repeated behaviour.
example: A notification creates curiosity; opening the app briefly relieves it.
action: Map one routine from signal to payoff.
scene: Phone notification, an adult glances at the phone, opens it and then reflects beside a notebook.
narration: Look for the signal, desire, action and payoff behind a repeated behaviour. Map one routine from signal to payoff.

title: Notice your autopilot
idea: You can change a routine more deliberately after noticing it.
example: Record what happens between closing your laptop and going to bed.
action: Write down five routines you usually overlook.
scene: An adult observes their evening routine and records simple symbols on blank paper.
narration: You can change a routine more deliberately after noticing it. Write down five routines you usually overlook.

title: Give your action a clear cue
idea: Choose a definite moment or attach the action to an existing routine.
example: After watering the plant, clear one item from the desk.
action: Complete: After ___, I will ___.
scene: An adult waters a small plant then immediately clears one object from their desk.
narration: Choose a definite moment or attach the action to an existing routine. Complete: After ___, I will ___.

title: Let your surroundings remind you
idea: Place helpful cues where the action should happen.
example: Put a language-practice card beside the kettle.
action: Move one helpful cue into view.
scene: An adult places a study card beside a kettle, then picks it up while water heats.
narration: Place helpful cues where the action should happen. Move one helpful cue into view.

title: Remove unnecessary temptation
idea: Reduce exposure to cues that trigger an unwanted routine.
example: Place the game controller in a drawer before a study session.
action: Remove one cue before the next difficult moment.
scene: An adult puts a game controller in a closed drawer, then sits at a quiet study desk.
narration: Reduce exposure to cues that trigger an unwanted routine. Remove one cue before the next difficult moment.

title: Make the routine appealing
idea: Connect a useful action with something you enjoy.
bullets: Pair a useful and enjoyable activity.
example: Listen to a favourite instrumental playlist while sorting paperwork.
action: Choose a pleasure that fits your useful action.
scene: An adult puts on headphones and happily sorts a small stack of papers.
narration: Connect a useful action with something you enjoy. Choose a pleasure that fits your useful action.

title: Choose a supportive social setting
idea: People around you help define what feels normal.
example: Join a weekly sketching circle where practising is normal.
action: Find one group that already practises your chosen behaviour.
scene: Three adult friends sit at a shared table sketching simple objects together.
narration: People around you help define what feels normal. Find one group that already practises your chosen behaviour.

title: Find the need behind the habit
idea: An unwanted action may be an attempt to meet a real need.
bullets: Try a better response to that need.
example: If shopping follows loneliness, test calling a friend before browsing.
action: Name the need and one alternative response.
scene: An adult pauses while browsing a shopping page and chooses to call a friend.
narration: An unwanted action may be an attempt to meet a real need. Name the need and one alternative response.

title: Practise instead of only preparing
idea: Repetition builds familiarity; endless planning can delay action.
example: Record a short spoken sentence rather than collecting more speaking tips.
action: Do one small real attempt now.
scene: An adult closes a pile of notes and records one spoken sentence into a desk microphone.
narration: Repetition builds familiarity; endless planning can delay action. Do one small real attempt now.

title: Remove steps from the good habit
idea: An action is easier to repeat when fewer obstacles stand in its way.
example: Leave drawing tools arranged on a tray after practice.
action: Remove one setup step.
scene: An adult arranges pencils and a sketchpad neatly so the next drawing session starts immediately.
narration: An action is easier to repeat when fewer obstacles stand in its way. Remove one setup step.

title: Start with a two-minute version
idea: Make the beginning so small that showing up feels manageable.
bullets: Let it lead to a larger routine.
example: Open the language app and practise one sound.
action: Write the smallest honest version of your habit.
scene: An adult opens a language lesson and carefully speaks a single sound.
narration: Make the beginning so small that showing up feels manageable. Write the smallest honest version of your habit.

title: Prepare your future choice
idea: Make a useful decision in advance so you need fewer later decisions.
example: Set an app timer before the evening starts.
action: Set one reversible commitment for tomorrow.
scene: An adult sets a screen-time timer, places the phone down and begins a calm evening routine.
narration: Make a useful decision in advance so you need fewer later decisions. Set one reversible commitment for tomorrow.

title: Give progress an immediate payoff
idea: A small positive finish can help a useful action feel worth repeating.
bullets: Avoid rewards that undo the purpose.
example: After tidying one shelf, pause to enjoy the clear space.
action: Choose a small satisfying finish.
scene: An adult tidies one shelf, steps back and enjoys the clean space.
narration: A small positive finish can help a useful action feel worth repeating. Choose a small satisfying finish.

title: Make consistency visible
idea: A simple record helps you notice repetition and recover after a lapse.
bullets: Check quality as well as counts.
example: Mark each completed pronunciation practice; note one sound that improved.
action: Record today’s action, then plan the next chance.
scene: An adult marks a calendar, notices a missed square and calmly marks the next completed day.
narration: A simple record helps you notice repetition and recover after a lapse. Record today’s action, then plan the next chance.

title: Use supportive accountability
idea: A clear agreement with another person can make follow-through more noticeable.
example: Tell a study partner which session you will complete and when you will report back.
action: Write one precise check-in agreement.
scene: Two adults agree on a practice session, then one checks in after completing it.
narration: A clear agreement with another person can make follow-through more noticeable. Write one precise check-in agreement.

title: Choose a practice that fits you
idea: Your strengths and preferences can help you choose a promising field of effort.
bullets: Fit is useful; effort still matters.
example: Test sketching, audio editing and writing; compare energy and progress.
action: Try two approaches and compare your response.
scene: An adult tries sketching, recording and writing at three small workspaces.
narration: Your strengths and preferences can help you choose a promising field of effort. Try two approaches and compare your response.

title: Keep the challenge manageable
idea: A task just beyond your current ability can keep practice engaging.
example: Practise a slightly harder rhythm after a basic one becomes easy.
action: Make one small adjustment to difficulty.
scene: An adult musician practises a simple rhythm, then tries a slightly more demanding rhythm.
narration: A task just beyond your current ability can keep practice engaging. Make one small adjustment to difficulty.

title: Review the routine to keep improving
idea: Automatic repetition can hide mistakes; reflection and focused practice help you improve.
example: Review a recording, identify one unclear sound, and practise it deliberately.
action: Choose one routine to review this week.
scene: An adult listens to their own recording, notices one weak point and carefully repeats it.
narration: Automatic repetition can hide mistakes; reflection and focused practice help you improve. Choose one routine to review this week.
